original_poem:
केसरिया बालम, पधारो म्हारे देश,  
मरुधरा री धरती पर, प्रेम रा फेरो।  
प्यार री पावन बण, रेती री माटी,  
बांध्यो म्हारी कलाई पर सुहाग री रेगो।
translated_poem:
Beloved in saffron, come to my land,  
To Marudhara's soil, where love makes its stand.  
A holy bond in sands of gold,  
A bracelet of love, forever we hold.

stanzas.loss_note: 'सुहाग री रेगो' (thread of marital auspiciousness) loses its specific bridal-ritual and suhag connotation, rendered as generic love bracelet.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: love as a sacred forest or bond — the desert sands transformed into a holy, sheltering space of union
golden desert sand as the consecrated ground of a love that is both earthly and spiritually pure
the thread of marital auspiciousness as the binding promise of the beloved's return and union

cultural_entities.translation_note: The iconic Rajasthani folk song title and its saffron-clad beloved imagery is partially preserved but the folk-song tradition identity is lost in translation.
Marudhara (land of the dead/desert) rendered as generic soil; its specific Thar desert cultural identity is weakened.
Suhag (marital auspiciousness thread) is a specific bridal ritual custom flattened to 'bracelet of love'.
